paper_id: Why Do Neural Dialog Systems Generate Short and Meaningless Replies_ A Comparison between Dialog and Translation
title: Why Do Neural Dialog Systems Generate Short and Meaningless Replies? A Comparison between Dialog and Translation
motivation: Neural dialog systems generate universal short replies like 'I don't know', which is a severe practical failure.
problem_framing: Compare dialog vs translation Seq2Seq behavior; hypothesis: unaligned data (multiple plausible replies) causes collapse.
key_insight: Shuffling translation pairs creates unaligned distribution, reproducing short replies—confirming the conjecture.
method_signature: Shuffle source-target pairs in translation to mimic dialog's multiple-plausible-replies property.
evaluation_criteria: BLEU, length, negative log-probability, entropy, R^2 correlation of hidden states with time step.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: 100% shuffle shows anomalous high R^2; no good explanation currently.
evidence_for_taste: admittedly impossible to construct exactly the same scenario
causally expressed in our previous work
thinking_moves: 把dialog问题转译成translation可控实验
通过人为制造unaligned数据验证假设
承认实验无法完全复现dialog的真实场景
extraction_notes: First author is Bolin Wei; Ge Li is co-author withSoftware Institute affiliation.
